reasoning: x divides x^3 + x^2 + 16, and x already divides x^3 and x^2, so x must divide 16. Positive divisors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 — exactly 5 values. Verified by brute force over x = 1..200.
30 = 2·3·5, three distinct primes each to the first power. Each prime goes wholly into exactly one of a, b, c, giving 3^3 = 27 ordered triples. Brute-force count over all factorisations confirms 27.
Real roots require discriminant >= 0: 16 + 4·log10(N) >= 0, so log10(N) >= -4, i.e. N >= 10^-4 = 1/10000. Minimum N = 1/10000.
Positive-integer solutions of x + y + z = 12 number C(11,2) = 55. Direct enumeration gives 55.

With a = n, b = n+1, c = n(n+1): I = n^2 + (n+1)^2 + n^2(n+1)^2 = (n^2 + n + 1)^2. Since n^2 + n = n(n+1) is even, n^2+n+1 is odd. Checked n = -5..7: I is always a perfect square of an odd number (9, 49, 169, 441, 961, ...).
The smallest odd composite number is 9. Digit sum of 23P62971335 is 41 + P; need 41 + P divisible by 9, and 41 mod 9 = 5, so P = 4. Verified: 23462971335 mod 9 = 0.
Unit digits of powers of 3 cycle 3, 9, 7, 1 with period 4. 99 mod 4 = 3, giving the third entry, 7. Verified: pow(3, 99, 10) = 7.

LCM = 28·HCF and HCF + LCM = 1740 give 29·HCF = 1740, HCF = 60, LCM = 1680. Product of the numbers = 60·1680 = 100800, so the other number = 100800/240 = 420. Check: gcd(240,420) = 60 and lcm(240,420) = 1680, both consistent.
x^n - a^n = (x - a)(x^(n-1) + x^(n-2)a + ... + a^(n-1)) holds for every natural number n, odd or even. Options B, C, D are unnecessarily restrictive.
Each term rationalises to sqrt(k+1) - sqrt(k), so the sum telescopes to sqrt(100) - sqrt(1) = 10 - 1 = 9. Sympy evaluates the 99-term sum to exactly 9.
Inner: sqrt(x) = x^(1/2); x·x^(1/2) = x^(3/2); sqrt of that = x^(3/4); x·x^(3/4) = x^(7/4); 14th root gives x^(7/56) = x^(1/8). Sympy: log of the expression to base x is 1/8.

For the ten numbers ±1..±5 the sum S = 0 and the sum of squares = 2(1+4+9+16+25) = 110. Pairwise product sum = (S^2 - sum of squares)/2 = (0 - 110)/2 = -55. Brute-force over all C(10,2) pairs gives -55.
Total distance to clear = 110 + 165 = 275 m. Speed = 132 km/hr = 132·5/18 = 110/3 m/s. Time = 275/(110/3) = 15/2 = 7.5 s (exact rational check).
SI = P/4 = P·R·T/100 with R = T = n gives n^2/100 = 1/4, so n^2 = 25, n = 5.
Same total writing space: 60n = (60+10)(n-3) = 70n - 210, so 10n = 210 and n = 21.
x men × x hours/day × x days = x^3 man-hours produce x units, so the rate is 1/x^2 units per man-hour. y men × y hours × y days = y^3 man-hours produce k = y^3/x^2 = y^3 x^(-2) units.
d(5) = 2, d(11) = 2, d(55) = 4, d(16) = 5. Statement 1: 2 = 2, true. Statement 2: 2·2 = 4 = d(55), true. Statement 3: 2 + 2 = 4 ≠ 5, false. So 1 and 2 only.

Statement 1 is false: for n = 1, A_1 = 2 + 1 = 3, which is prime (also 7, 31, 211, 2311 are prime). P_n contains the factor 2 so P_n is even, making A_n odd; hence A_n + 2 is odd (statement 2 true) and A_n + 1 is even (statement 3 true). Verified for n = 1..12.

The balance reads 1000 gm when only 800 gm is actually delivered, so the customer pays the cost price of 1000 gm while receiving goods costing 800 gm. Profit = 200/800 = 25%. Runner-up A (20%): that wins if the fraction is taken on the marked-up (selling) quantity 1000 instead of the shopkeeper's outlay 800, i.e. 200/1000. Profit percentage is by convention computed on cost, so 25%.
In one minute the water advances 2000/60 = 100/3 m. Volume = 3 × 40 × 100/3 = 4000 m^3 = 4000 × 1000 = 40,00,000 litres.
x = 0.72C (28% loss), y = 1.12C (12% profit). y : x = 1.12 : 0.72 = 112 : 72 = 14 : 9. Sympy confirms the ratio is exactly 14/9.
300/v - 300/(v+15) = 1 gives v^2 + 15v - 4500 = 0, so v = 60 (rejecting -75). Check: 300/60 = 5 h and 300/75 = 4 h, one hour less.

With x = ky: (1) (x^2+y^2)/(x^2-y^2) = (k^2+1)/(k^2-1), a constant, so it varies as; (2) x/y^2 = k/y, i.e. varies inversely as y — sympy confirms (x/y^2)·y = k; (3) (x^4 y^2)^(1/(2n)) = ((x^2 y)^2)^(1/(2n)) = (x^2 y)^(1/n), the two expressions are identical so their ratio is 1. All three hold. Runner-up B (2 and 3 only): statement 1 fails only in the degenerate case k = ±1, where x^2 - y^2 ≡ 0 and 'varies as' is undefined; if the examiner counts that edge case as a failure, B would win.
Ena is 13; mother = 13 + 24 = 37; father = 37 + 3 = 40. Ena was born 4 years after the marriage, so the marriage was 13 + 4 = 17 years ago. Father's age then = 40 - 17 = 23.
Mahesh 60; Ram = 60 - 5 = 55; Raju = 55 - 4 = 51; Babu = 51 - 6 = 45. Difference Mahesh - Babu = 60 - 45 = 15.
N(1 + x/100)(1 - x/100) = N(1 - x^2/10000), which is less than N by N·x^2/10000 for any non-zero x, independent of N.

From ab + xy - xb = 0: ab = x(b - y), so x/a = b/(b-y). From bc + yz - cy = 0: c(b - y) = -yz, so c/z = -y/(b-y). Sum = (b - y)/(b - y) = 1. Sympy solve for x and c then simplifying x/a + c/z returns exactly 1.
Product of the polynomials = HCF × LCM. LCM factors as (2x+1)(3x+1)(5x-3) and the given polynomial is (2x+1)(3x+1). Other = (3x+1)(2x+1)(3x+1)(5x-3)/((2x+1)(3x+1)) = (3x+1)(5x-3) = 15x^2 - 4x - 3.
Subtracting the two equations gives 4(2q - 1) = 0, so q = 1/2 and 2q - 1 = 0. Then the left side is 0, so 2pq - 10 = 0 and pq = 5. Sympy returns p = 10, q = 1/2, pq = 5.
Sympy simplifies the whole expression to 6/(a + c). Numeric spot checks: at (a,c) = (5,2) it is 6/7, at (7,3) it is 3/5 = 6/10 — both matching 6/(a+c).
(2x^2 + 2x - 1)^2 = 4x^4 + 8x^3 + (4x^2 - 4x^2) - 4x + 1 = 4x^4 + 8x^3 - 4x + 1, an exact match. All three other options were squared and none equals the target.
(10a+b) - (10b+a) = 9(a-b) = 27, so a - b = 3; with a + b = 13, a = 8 and b = 5. The number is 85 and the product of digits is 40. Enumeration over all two-digit numbers finds only 85.

Setting each ratio equal to k: x = k(b+c), y = k(c+a), z = k(b-a). Then x - y - z = k[(b+c) - (c+a) - (b-a)] = 0. Sympy evaluates the other three options to 2k(b+c), 2k(a+c) and k(-a+4b+3c), none identically zero.
Measure time from X's start. Y overtakes X when 4T = 5(T - 2), so T = 10 h. Z must overtake at the same T: 4·10 = 6(10 - s) gives s = 10/3 h after X, i.e. 10/3 - 2 = 4/3 hours after Y.

1 - x - x^n + x^(n+1) = (1-x) - x^n(1-x) = (1-x)(1-x^n) = (1-x)^2 (1 + x + ... + x^(n-1)). Sympy: the remainder on division by (1-x)^2 is 0 for n = 1..7, while the remainder on division by (1+x)^2 is non-zero.
Profit 75 - x equals x% of the outlay x: 75 - x = x^2/100, so x^2 + 100x - 7500 = 0 and x = 50. Check: cost 50, profit 25, which is 50% of 50.

value: x(t - y)t/y  (the DISTANCE of the journey)
reasoning: STEM ODDITY, solved as printed: 'How long was the journey?' reads as a time, and the time t is already given — but every option is an expression whose value is a distance, so the quantity asked for must be the distance. With d = vt and d = (v+x)(t-y), sympy gives d = x·t·(t-y)/y, which is exactly option B (x(t-y)·t·y^-1). Dimensional check kills the others: A and D are km·h^2, C is km/h; only B has units of km. The time reading would give the answer 't', which is not an option at all.
t = k·sqrt(d) with 4 = k·sqrt(78.40). Then t = 4·sqrt(122.50/78.40) = 4·sqrt(1.5625) = 4 × 1.25 = 5 seconds (exact rational check: 1225/784 = (5/4)^2).

Taking log10: (3-4x)(log2+log3) + (x+5)(2log2) = 3log2. With the given values log6 = 0.778, log4 = 0.602, log8 = 0.903: 5.344 - 2.510x = 0.903, so x = 4441/2510 ≈ 1.7693. An independent exact numerical root of 6^(3-4x)·4^(x+5) = 8 is 1.76920, and f(1) > 0 > f(2), confirming the root lies strictly between 1 and 2.
The Euclidean algorithm computes the greatest common divisor (HCF) of two integers by repeated division with remainder. It has nothing to do with roots or squares.
For rational r ≠ 0, surface area 4πr^2 and volume (4/3)πr^3 are each a non-zero rational multiple of the irrational π, hence irrational. Neither statement holds.

m = cos^2θ/sinθ and n = sin^2θ/cosθ, so mn = sinθcosθ. The expression = (mn)^(2/3)(m^(2/3) + n^(2/3)); and m^(2/3) + n^(2/3) = (cos^2θ + sin^2θ)/(sinθcosθ)^(2/3) = 1/(sinθcosθ)^(2/3), so the product is exactly 1. Numerically confirmed to 20 digits at θ = 0.3, 0.9, 1.2 rad (values outside the first quadrant only give complex artefacts from real cube roots of negatives).

With c = cosθ, k = c + 1/c so k^2 - 4 = c^2 + 1/c^2 - 2 = (1-c^2)^2/c^2. And sin^2θ - tan^2θ = -sin^4θ/cos^2θ = -(1-c^2)^2/c^2 = -(k^2-4) = 4 - k^2. Checked numerically at θ = 0.3, 0.9, 1.2, 2.0, -0.7 rad: the value is always negative and always equals 4 - k^2, ruling out option C.
An angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle C = 90° and A + B = 90°. cos 90° + sin 90° = 0 + 1 = 1.
For real x ≠ 0, x + 1/x has minimum 2 for x > 0 and maximum -2 for x < 0 (sympy confirms), so |x + 1/x| ≥ 2. Both sinθ and cosθ lie in [-1, 1], so neither equation is possible for any real x.
Interior angle of a regular pentagon = (5-2)·180/5 = 108°, and 108° = 108π/180 = 3π/5 radian.
Sum = 5π/12 rad = 75°, difference = 15°, so the angles are 45° and 30°. k = 45/30 = 3/2.

Statement 1: 2sin^2θ - cosθ + 4 = 0 reduces to 2cos^2θ + cosθ - 6 = 0 with roots cosθ = 3/2 and -2, neither in [-1,1], so the equation holds for NO θ — statement 1 is false. Statement 2: on (0, π/2) sympy gives min(tanθ + cotθ) = 2 (AM-GM), so it cannot be less than 2 — true.
sinθ has maximum 1, so max(3sinθ - 4) = 3 - 4 = -1. Sympy maximum confirms -1.

sinθ + cosθ = √2 squares to 1 + 2sinθcosθ = 2, so sinθcosθ = 1/2 and sin^2θcos^2θ = 1/4. sin^6θ + cos^6θ = 1 - 3sin^2θcos^2θ = 1/4, plus 6 × 1/4 = 3/2, total 7/4. Direct evaluation at θ = π/4 gives 1.75.
9sin^2θ + 16cos^2θ = 9 + 7cos^2θ, minimised when cos^2θ = 0, giving 9. Sympy minimum confirms 9.

cos^2 47 - sin^2 47 = (cos47 + sin47)(cos47 - sin47) = k(cos47 - sin47), and (cos47 - sin47)^2 = 2 - k^2. Since 47° > 45°, sin47 > cos47 so the second factor is negative: cos47 - sin47 = -√(2 - k^2). Numerically cos^2 47 - sin^2 47 = -0.0697565 = -k√(2-k^2) exactly; note k^2 ≈ 1.9976 > 1, so options C and D take the square root of a negative number and are invalid.

p^3 = cos^2θ/sinθ and q^3 = sin^2θ/cosθ, so q^3/p^3 = (sin^2θ/cosθ)·(sinθ/cos^2θ) = tan^3θ, giving tanθ = q/p. Numeric check at θ = 0.3, 0.9, 1.2 rad: q/p matches tanθ to 15 digits while p/q and pq do not.
With 0 ≤ α, β ≤ 90°, α - β lies in [-90°, 90°] and cos(α - β) = 1 forces α - β = 0, i.e. α = β. Then sinα - sinβ + cosα - cosβ = 0.
sin29° = cos61°, so statement 1's expression is 2cos61° = 0.96962, which does not exceed 1 — true. cot67° = tan23°, so statement 2's expression is exactly 0, which is not less than 0 — false.

Angle B = 90° gives AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2. Substituting into AB^2 + BC^2 + CD^2 - AD^2 = 0 gives AC^2 + CD^2 = AD^2, so by the converse of Pythagoras triangle ACD is right-angled at C, i.e. angle ACD = 90°.
The internal bisector from A divides BC in the ratio of the adjacent sides: BD/DC = AB/AC = 16/12 = 4/3. With BD = 4, DC = 4 × 3/4 = 3 cm.

P, Q, R, S all lie on the same circle, and the bisector feet occur in the same cyclic order as A, B, C, D, so PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in which angle PQR and angle RSP are opposite angles — they sum to 180°. Verified by arc computation for four different cyclic quadrilaterals (including the square), each giving angle PQR = angle RSP = 90° and sum 180°.

With side a and BD = a/3, the cosine rule in triangle ABD (angle B = 60°) gives AD^2 = a^2 + a^2/9 - 2·a·(a/3)·(1/2) = 7a^2/9. So AD^2 : AB^2 = 7 : 9. Coordinate check with B(0,0), C(1,0), A(0.5, √3/2), D(1/3, 0) gives 0.7778 = 7/9.

1: in a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, triangles AOB and COD formed by the diagonals are similar, so AO/OC = BO/OD — the diagonals divide each other proportionally. 2: a line parallel to the parallel sides cuts each of the two triangles formed by a diagonal proportionally (basic proportionality theorem), so it divides the non-parallel sides in the same ratio. Both true.

With V = (1/3)πr^2H and C = πrl, l^2 = r^2 + H^2: 3πVH^3 = π^2 r^2 H^4 and 9V^2 = π^2 r^4 H^2, so the sum is π^2 r^2 H^2 (H^2 + r^2) = (πrl)^2 H^2 = C^2H^2. Sympy confirms the ratio of the sum to C^2H^2 is exactly 1.
Small ball radius = 1 mm = 0.1 cm; big ball radius 8 cm. Volumes scale as the cube of the radius: (8/0.1)^3 = 80^3 = 512000.

Let the diagonals be d and d+2. Side = √(d^2+(d+2)^2)/2, so perimeter = 2√(d^2+(d+2)^2) = (2d+2) + 6. Solving gives d = 6, diagonals 6 and 8 (side 5, perimeter 20 = 14 + 6 ✓). Area = (1/2)(6)(8) = 24.

In a right triangle the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, so hypotenuse = 2 × 5 = 10 cm. Area = (1/2) × base(hypotenuse) × altitude = (1/2)(10)(4) = 20 cm^2. (The altitude 4 ≤ 5 = max possible, so the configuration exists.)
The angles are 180·part/total. A: total 6 → 30, 60, 90 ✓. B: total 12 → 45, 60, 75 ✓. C: total 18 → 50, 60, 70 ✓. D: total 21 → 360/7, 60, 480/7 — not integers. So 6:7:8 cannot be the proportion.
New area factor = 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99 = 99/100 exactly, a 1% decrease.
Surface areas 4πr^2 in ratio 1:4 give radii in ratio 1:2; volumes (4/3)πr^3 then go as 1^3 : 2^3 = 1 : 8.
The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°, so (n-2)·180 = 720, giving n - 2 = 4 and n = 6 — a hexagon.
11 km = 1,100,000 cm over 5000 revolutions gives a circumference of 220 cm. 2 × (22/7) × r = 220 gives r = 35 cm.
Diameters (hence radii) 4:5, volumes 1:4. V ∝ r^2h, so (16h1)/(25h2) = 1/4, giving h1/h2 = 25/64.
2πr = 4a gives a = πr/2. Ratio of areas = πr^2 / (π^2r^2/4) = 4/π. Sympy simplifies to 4/π.
With sides a, a+2, a+4: a^2 + (a+2)^2 = (a+4)^2 gives a^2 - 4a - 12 = 0, so a = 6 and the sides are 6, 8, 10. Product = 480. Search over even a up to 60 finds only this triple.
OM ⊥ AB and ON ⊥ AC (radius to point of contact), so in quadrilateral AMON the angles at M and N are each 90°. Angle MON = 360° - 90° - 90° - 70° = 110°.
For a right triangle a^2 + b^2 = c^2, so the sum of the squares of all three sides is 2c^2 = 8450, giving c^2 = 4225 and c = 65.
Equal bases b and equal areas: (1/2)·b·(k·h_p) = b·h_p gives k = 2.
Areas in ratio m^2 : n^4 give sides in ratio √(m^2) : √(n^4) = m : n^2, and perimeters are 4 × side, so the same ratio m : n^2.

value: Area of triangle PAB is equal to area of triangle PAC
reasoning: AD is a median so BD = DC, hence [ABD] = [ACD] (same altitude from A) and [PBD] = [PCD] (same altitude from P). Subtracting, [PAB] = [ABD] - [PBD] = [ACD] - [PCD] = [PAC].
Segment = sector - triangle = (1/2)r^2θ - (1/2)r^2 sinθ = (1/2)r^2(θ - sinθ), and sinθ = 2 sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2). Sympy confirms the difference from option B is identically 0.

With C at the origin, A = (a,0), B = (0,b), P = (p,0), Q = (0,q): AQ^2 + BP^2 = (a^2+q^2) + (b^2+p^2) = (a^2+b^2) + (p^2+q^2) = AB^2 + PQ^2, so statement 1 is always true (verified at four random configurations). Statement 2, AB = 2PQ, depends on where P and Q are and fails in general (checked numerically), so it is false.

Adjacent coins touch, so the square's side is 2r. Each vertex contributes a quarter-circle inside the square, total covered = 4 × (1/4)πr^2 = πr^2. Uncovered = 4r^2 - (22/7)r^2 = (6/7)r^2 = 42, so r^2 = 49 and r = 7 cm.
The bucket is a frustum with R = 2x, r = x, h = 3x. V = (πh/3)(R^2 + Rr + r^2) = (22/7)(3x/3)(4x^2 + 2x^2 + x^2) = (22/7)·x·7x^2 = 22x^3.
s = 2(pq + qr + rp) and t = pqr, so 1/p + 1/q + 1/r = (qr + rp + pq)/pqr = (s/2)/t = s/(2t). Sympy confirms the difference is exactly 0.

STEM ODDITY, solved as printed (and verified against the page image, which does read 'Fifteen candidates' with only ten marks listed): the ten marks given are those of the candidates who PASSED, so the other five failed and must have scored below the lowest passing mark, 4. Sorted, the fifteen marks are [five failing marks ≤ 4], 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9. The median is the 8th value = 6. This holds whatever the five failing marks are, since all five sit at or below 4.
Sorted: 111, 141, 154, 175, 176, 180, 191. With 7 values the median is the 4th, which is 175 gm.

The 'average' shoe size a shop needs is the size sold most often; the arithmetic/geometric mean can give a non-existent size and the median ignores the demand peak. The mode is the measure used for such categorical/most-frequent data.
In a histogram the AREA of each rectangle is proportional to the frequency; when all class widths are equal the height is therefore proportional to (and taken as) the frequency of the class.

AMBIGUOUS BASELINE, solved as printed. Ages sum to 175, original mean = 25. After 5 years the seven ages sum to 210 (mean 30) and a new member aged x joins, giving mean (210 + x)/8. Reading 'the mean age of the family now goes up by 1·5 years' against the ORIGINAL mean: (210+x)/8 = 26.5 gives x = 2 = option B. Runner-up: the more literal reading — up by 1.5 from the mean immediately before the addition (30) — gives (210+x)/8 = 31.5, i.e. x = 42, which matches NO printed option; that reading would win if the examiner had intended the pre-addition baseline, but then the question would be defective. Only the original-mean baseline lands on an option, so B.
50b + 40(100 - b) = 46 × 100 = 4600 gives b = 60 boys and 40 girls; the excess is 20.

The algebraic sum of deviations about the arithmetic mean is identically zero: Σ(x_i - x̄) = Σx_i - n·x̄ = 0. Here the mean is exactly 45 (sum 450, n = 10) and the exact rational sum of deviations is 0.
Mean of the five = (5x + 20)/5 = x + 4 = m, so x = m - 4. Mean of the first three = (3x + 6)/3 = x + 2 = m - 4 + 2 = m - 2.
The list 2, 4, ..., 100 has 50 terms, so the median is the mean of the 25th and 26th terms, which are 50 and 52: (50 + 52)/2 = 51.
For two numbers GM^2 = AM × HM, so AM = 144/10 = 14.4. Consistency check: a + b = 28.8 and ab = 144 give real numbers 22.36 and 6.44, whose GM is 12 and HM is 2·144/28.8 = 10, as required.
